b: p

My boyfriend 31M & I 30F have been together for 2.5 years. After discovering his infidelity and deception, I initially wanted to end the relationship. I honestly wasn’t interested in CC, but I agreed because I hoped the process might help me rediscover the desire to be with him along with some tools to help me move forward.
p
I’m starting to feel like CC is keeping me in a constant state of emotional turmoil rather than helping me find clarity.
p

Our CC recommended that we have weekly check-ins and take personal days where we spend time independently and limit communication. My WP recently decided to use his personal day to travel out of town to handle his car registration. The problem is that the last time he traveled there alone, he cheated on me.
Naturally, this brought up a lot of anxiety.
p

During CC, the conversation seems to keep coming back to my childhood trauma, abandonment issues, and why I struggle to move on (trust blindly). CC also mentioned that if I’m spending so much time worrying about what my WP is doing, then I’m not occupying my time enough with other things.
p

I have my own interests, goals, routines, and things I’m working toward. I don’t feel like the issue is that I have nothing better to do than worry about a man. The issue is that I’m in a relationship with someone who has given me legitimate reasons to question his honesty so I think about this while doing the things.
p

What I don’t think is being fully understood is that sometimes the emotions are so overwhelming that I become stagnant and unproductive in other areas of my life. It’s not that I don’t have things to do or goals I want to accomplish. It’s that sometimes I’m so emotionally exhausted from everything surrounding this relationship that I struggle to show up for myself the way I want to.And that’s becoming another concern of mine. I have personal goals, things I want to accomplish, and a version of myself I’m trying to get back to. But some days I feel like so much of my emotional energy is being consumed by this relationship and the process of trying to repair it that I have very little left to give myself.
p

I don’t want my entire life to revolve around recovering from someone else’s betrayal. I didn’t enter this relationship feeling this way. My current anxiety and distrust developed because of things that happened within this relationship.
p

I’m not dismissing the possibility that my childhood can influence things. Which IC will be better to assist with that and I’m making arrangements to get that going. But I feel like there’s so much emphasis on why I can’t move past what happened and not enough emphasis on why I actually WANT to continue a relationship with someone who betrayed me and doesn’t make me feel emotionally safe.
p

Also this idea that consistency is supposed to rebuild trust. My BF being consistent was never necessarily the issue. Someone can communicate, be affectionate, follow routines, show up for you, and seemingly do everything right while still being deceptive behind your back. Which is the situation. Even if he does everything right moving forward, how do I know he’s not doing the same things behind my back? I understand that no relationship comes with absolute guarantees, but I’m starting to question whether I even want to put myself through the emotional work of learning to trust him again.
p

I don’t want to monitor his location or constantly check his phone. I don’t want to spend my days wondering if he’s being honest. And he doesn’t want to feel like he’s a prisoner to my healing or that he has to constantly prove himself.
p
I just want peace. And the more I think about it, the more I wonder whether what I actually need is separation rather than reconciliation.
p

I want to get myself together emotionally, mentally, and personally. I want to be able to pursue my goals without feeling like I’m constantly trying to recover from something happening in my relationship. I want the freedom to figure out what I want without simultaneously feeling responsible for maintaining a relationship I’m not even sure I want anymore.
p
I’m trying to rebuild myself emotionally while remaining in the same relationship that caused so much of this pain. And sometimes it feels like the process itself is prolonging my distress.
p

The complicated part is that we still have nine months remaining on our lease. So even if I decide that separation is what I need, there are financial and logistical realities that make it difficult to simply walk away and start fresh.
p

And I think that’s part of what makes everything feel so heavy. I know that regardless of what I decide, this isn’t going to be an overnight process. Whether we reconcile, separate while still sharing financial responsibilities, or eventually go our separate ways, there’s still a long road ahead.
p

I’ve expressed in CC that I currently don’t feel like I want to be with him, but that I’m participating because I’m hoping those feelings might change. I understand that being triggered doesn’t automatically mean reconciliation isn’t working. And I can acknowledge that maybe I am struggling to let go of certain things.
p

I don’t want to confuse staying and enduring emotional distress with doing the work to heal. And I don’t want to spend months or years trying to convince myself of something that I may have already emotionally checked out of.
p
**For those who have been through couples counseling after infidelity:**
p

Did counseling initially make you feel worse before things got better?
Did you ever feel like the focus shifted more toward your reactions, trauma, or inability to trust than the betrayal itself?
Have you experienced the emotional weight of reconciliation affecting your productivity, motivation, or ability to focus on yourself?
How did you determine whether you genuinely wanted reconciliation versus just wanting the relationship to work because of the time and love you’d invested?
Has anyone chosen separation while still having a shared lease or financial obligations? How did you navigate that?
p
I’m genuinely confused. I don’t necessarily think my BF is incapable of changing.I’m just starting to wonder whether I want to be part of the process anymore.
p

I feel like I’m spending so much time trying to figure out how to feel safe with him again that I’m still compromising so much for the relationship still. And somewhere in the middle of all this, I feel like I’m losing the energy I need to show up for myself.
